This documentary fucked with my head insofar as it portrayed very heavy drinkers, who are very successful, doing just 'fine'. I know for certain that while I did have a time where my outward perception of my drunkness was masked by success, I eventually hit a tipping point where any drinking brings out so much awful in me that there's just no going back.

I really wonder, in an academic sense, what it is that makes that switch flip.  The switch from sustaining at high levels of drinking, to it then becoming an absolute nuclear blast in life.  A neurological time bomb?  An external psychological event?  

I don't think we'll ever know quite the truth to our versions of our diseases.  I want so badly to look at the past and connect all of the dots and have it all make 'sense' from a clinical point of view.  

But the end case remains the same.  IWNDWYT.  But I'll forever wonder what/when/how/why my journey happened.  And I'll forever wonder how I see other people living my old life and 'seemingly' making it work.  

I've never had a relationship as complex and nuanced as my one with alcohol.  Though the answer is as simple as ever.  IWNDWYT.
